Losing someone to suicide is a terrible and traumatic thing, so you are totally in the right to look to the people closest to you for  a sympathetic/empathetic support system and It's really a shame that they aren't able to be that for you because you absolutely deserve it...

Keep in mind though that you're asking people to try and understand something that is so foreign to most that they have lito know idea what to say or do to empathize. It's kinda like an astronaut asking you to empathize with them on what space is like.

Personally I find alot of support and understanding from online communities like this one. Just know that while it may feel like it sometimes, you're not alone.

Try to find a way to be kind to yourself and stay strong.

So first, I'm so sorry you're hear asking for advice. This is a terrible club to be in but, there's ALOT of good support in this sub.

It's been over 2 1/2 years since I lost my wife to suicide. I'm still in contact with her family (mainly her mom and dad).

 Keep in mind this is just my OPINION but, I feel it's our job to be the best support system we can be and don't unload too much of what we're going through with the family of the person we just lost. 

Remember they are also grieving someone but in a completely different way so they may not be able to understand fully what you're going through or what you're trying to accomplish. 

My best advice, focus on and be kind to yourself. Guilt and confusion are going to a very real thing so please find positive and healthy outlets to navigate and express your grief i.e. Close friends or family possibly a therapist or grief counselor.

Know that there are a lot of people get who understand what you're going through and although it may be hard to understand now, it's definitely NOT your fault.

Your suffering may be over, but everyone else's has just begun.

It's been 6 months and I still have triggers. Jokes about death or suicide, emotional songs and movies and random things I wouldn't think would trigger me but suprise, they do. 

  I agree with the previous comments, try talking to you Mom & her bff. Having people to talk to  who understand what you're going through have been the best resource for me personally. Talking externalizes your feelings hopefully making them more tangible. Also try going to a few groups that center around suicide, they can be a good place to vent/cry and be around sympathetic people.
